title: Amendments of RFC 7643 / RFC 7644 by RFC 9865 / RFC 9967
description: Curated list of places where a newer RFC (9865 cursor pagination, 9967 SCIM events; both say 'Updates: 7643, 7644') adds to, changes, relaxes or replaces something an older RFC defines. Candidates are generated mechanically (amendment-candidates.json, find_amendment_candidates.py); classifying them is judgment, so entries start as 'proposed' and are checked mechanically by check_amendments.py (quotes exist at the cited lines, target sections exist, target records lie in the target section, every candidate is covered once). Line numbers are 1-based and refer to the rfcNNNN-fixed.txt files. Implementers should apply an amendment only when its 'condition' holds: most amendments add requirements that apply only if an optional feature is used (cursor pagination, asynchronous requests).

not_amendments.description: Candidates that turned out to be plain references or reuse of an older definition.

candidate.description: Candidate id from amendment-candidates.json, for example 'C9865-004'.

candidates.description: Candidate ids (amendment-candidates.json) this amendment covers; every candidate must be covered exactly once across 'amendments' and 'not_amendments'.

target.description: The older definition that is amended.

section.description: Section of the older RFC; must exist.

quote.description: Verbatim passage from rfcOLD-fixed.txt inside 'lines': the text that is added to or changed.

subject.description: Attribute, parameter or structure concerned, for example 'count'.

records.description: Record numbers 'n' of the affected keyword records in normative-rfcOLD.json (all inside 'section'); empty if the amendment only adds something new.

relation.description: 'extends': the newer RFC adds something next to the old requirement, which stays fully valid. 'modifies': the newer RFC changes or relaxes an older requirement under a condition. 'supersedes': the older requirement no longer applies at all (unconditional); expected to be rare.

condition.description: When the newer rule applies, for example 'when cursor-based pagination is used'. Required (non-empty) for 'modifies' and 'supersedes'.

effect.description: One sentence: what changes for an implementer.

status.description: 'proposed' until a person has checked the entry.
